item.title: Mechanochemically Disordered Li 2 Ta 2 OCl 10 Oxyhalide Unlocks Superionic Conductivity (>10 mS.cm −1 )
item.description:

Advanced Energy Materials | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 Novelty: A new lithium tantalum oxychloride, Li2Ta2OCl10, synthesized via a low-temperature route; ball milling induces a disordered, liquid-like Li+ sublattice, boosting conductivity 5000-fold to 11 mS.cm−1 and lowering activation energy to 0.27 eV. Significance: It enables all-solid-state batteries with low polarization and excellent cycling stability, establishing the Li–M–O–Cl family as a promising design space for superionic conductors.
🏷 solid electrolyte · oxyhalide · superionic conductivity · ball milling · all-solid-state battery

item.title: Helical Keratin‐Derived Aqueous Binders for High‐Performance Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
item.description:

Advanced Energy Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in a biomass-derived aqueous binder crosslinking α-helical protein with PVA and glycerol, where the helical structure acts as a "molecular spring" to buffer volume expansion while polar N/O groups anchor polysulfides. Its significance is enabling green, multifunctional binder design that suppresses shuttling, accelerates kinetics, and delivers stable cycling (0.056% decay/cycle over 600 cycles), advancing practical lithium–sulfur batteries.
🏷 lithium-sulfur battery · aqueous binder · keratin · polysulfide shuttling · cycling stability
